title: Supertrees, Satay, and Singapore Mode
excerpt: My first day in Singapore began at 4:30 am and never really slowed down — from figuring out the double-decker buses to wandering Gardens by the Bay under a pink sunset.

photos.alt: Flower Dome conservatory at Gardens by the Bay at dusk, its white arched ribs glowing against a pink and blue sky, visitors walking the path toward the entrance
Compact budget hotel room in Singapore with two single beds, wood-effect floor, colourful hexagonal wall decor, and a wall-mounted TV
Red-and-white double-decker public bus pulling up to a stop on a busy Singapore street under a bright midday sky
Thick toast sandwich stuffed with egg, luncheon meat, and cheese on a blue tray at True Breakfast Taiwanese café, menu visible in the background
Two public signs on a tiled pillar: 'No Cycling at Walkway' above a bold yellow warning that illegally parked vehicles will be clamped for a $150 release fee
Helix Bridge's steel double-helix structure curving across Marina Bay toward Marina Bay Sands hotel on a clear sunny day, pedestrians walking the bridge
Plate of Fried Hokkien Mee with prawns, squid, and thick yellow noodles in a golden broth, served with chilli sauce and chopsticks at Satay by the Bay
